stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for models.
The updated engine also delivers higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating ongoing development and adoption of Apple's ML ecosystem.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) regarding fine-grained 3D spatial understanding.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries from RGB videos.
Utilizes novel Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to inject high-level geometric priors into the VLM architecture.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based inputs that struggle with complex scenes or occlusion.
The model utilizes a graph-based approach to enable flexible and precise control over multiple subjects simultaneously.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of simply reducing sycophancy in LLMs, proposing a need for structured resistance and compliance.
Investigates how LLMs distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
Identifies three structured dimensions governing how models revise their judgments based on external input.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) regarding 3D spatial understanding.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries from RGB videos.
Employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to enhance the model's ability to capture high-level geometric priors.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap between text and audio-language models in deep logical reasoning.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
Transfers advanced reasoning capabilities from a text-based teacher model to an audio-language student model.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a new family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically for African languages.
The models utilize the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several West and East African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech from religious texts, ensuring broad coverage and clear licensing.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: Addresses a critical scalability bottleneck in speculative decoding when using Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads.
The core issue is that MTP draft heads incur a linear cost with context length due to full attention over the KV cache at each draft step.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' method aims to mitigate this 'full-context draft-KV tax' to enable efficient operation at million-token contexts.

stories.title: Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB, Affecting Shizuku, libadb and Developers
stories.author: kitsumed.github.io via raymii
bullet_points: Android is reportedly planning to restrict On-Device ADB access in the near future.
This change is expected to negatively impact tools and frameworks like Shizuku and libadb.
The development suggests a potential shift in how developers interact with the Android operating system.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's existing MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has halted plans to implement a subscription fee for a feature on its smart glasses.
The feature in question allows users to hear each other more clearly and operates locally on the device.
The pause follows public backlash against the proposed monetization strategy.

stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: Meta's smart glasses are facing significant public backlash regarding privacy concerns.
The devices are being misused by bad actors to film unsuspecting strangers.
Concerns have been raised specifically about women becoming subjects of unwanted social media content.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight

The maneuver suggests a continued focus on recovery and operational refinement for the Starship program.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major social media platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are facing accusations of non-compliance.
Researchers claim these tech giants are failing to provide legally mandated data.
The issue highlights ongoing tensions between Big Tech and European regulatory/research bodies.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update focuses primarily on token efficiency rather than a massive jump in raw capability.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for many use cases.
This signals a market trend where efficiency and cost-effectiveness are becoming as important as peak performance in LLMs.

stories.title: Roku raises streaming stick prices by up to 60 percent
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Roku is significantly increasing the prices of its streaming sticks by up to 60%.
The company attributes the price hike to a shortage of RAM.
The announcement follows a period where the CEO had expressed optimism about the business.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for time-series explanation.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in black-box model interpretations.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables training in diverse environments by natively supporting harness-based agent inference.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent performance in visual reasoning, even when equivalent information is presented across text, diagram, and combined views.
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different input modalities (text vs. visual) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning capabilities in current models.
This highlights a key limitation in current multimodal AI, indicating that simply having multiple views does not guarantee consistent reasoning ability.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across state spaces of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
The research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for time-series explanation in machine learning.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by moving beyond mere 'sufficiency' to incorporate 'necessity' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent performance in visual reasoning, even when multiple input views (text, diagram, combined) are available.
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different input views expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning capabilities within VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, where strong text reasoning does not guarantee equivalent visual reasoning.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework to transform static clinical cases into structured, executable storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM medical education tools by moving beyond localized interactions (like Q&A) to full decision-centered learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to ground the game in clinical scenarios.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents when they rely on complex, proprietary inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex).
Enables training in diverse environments by natively supporting stateful, multi-process harness inference within open infrastructure.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of generating dynamic, physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language prompts.
Current methods struggle with ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in generative simulations.
The proposed GS-Agent leverages generative foundation models to automate the creation of complex virtual environments.

stories.title: Artificial Epanorthosis: Why large language models overuse a classical rhetorical figure, and how to mitigate it
stories.author: Federico Boggia
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit systematic overuse of 'epanorthosis,' a classical rhetorical self-correction figure.
The overuse is attributed to training data rich in promotional prose and RLHF rewarding confident phrasing.
The study suggests the left-to-right generation process contributes to this rhetorical pattern.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent code concepts across different programming languages (Python and Rust).
It uses a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying model architecture on code representations.
The study measures a comprehensive inventory of grammatical concepts (58 for Python, 57 for Rust) to determine if representations are consistent across the tested configurations.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for code development research involving sensitive data.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as an alternative to external cloud services.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents on longitudinal data preparation tasks.

bullet_points: Introduction of 'Inflect-Micro-v2', a new voice model.

stories.title: Open-Weight AI Is Having Its Kubernetes Moment — And Developers Need to Pay Attention
stories.author: jamilxt

It serves as a warning/call-to-action for developers to pay close attention to this trend.

stories.title: Building AI Agents for Regulated Industries: The Architecture of "Prepare, Don't Decide"
stories.author: ritik_makhija_4a77a468ef1
bullet_points: The article addresses the architectural challenges of building AI agents specifically for highly regulated industries.
It critiques the common tutorial trend of increasing agent autonomy, suggesting a different approach is needed.
The core concept revolves around a 'Prepare, Don't Decide' paradigm, implying constrained or advisory AI behavior.

stories.title: Dual-Tier Memory Architecture for AI Agents: How Local Vector Search Scales to 14,726 Memories Without Pinecone
stories.author: hypernexus
bullet_points: Proposes a dual-tier memory architecture specifically designed for scaling AI agent memory.
Demonstrates the ability to handle a large number of memories (14,726) using local vector search.
Offers an alternative to relying on external, managed vector databases like Pinecone for memory storage.
